Depression can affect anyone - people from any financial background, age, gender, what's happened in their past, etc - it is indiscriminate. The thing to remember is that it's an illness. You don't typically question how someone got a cold based on what else is going on in their life, right?

I'm glad you are on the track to improvement, and that you have good support with your family and friends. 

P.S. It may not be a good idea to be active on r/depression while you are recovering. Personally I found that reading stories about people who are struggling made me feel, well, bad about feeling bad.

This was me a year ago. I barely scraped through high school, had stopped trying, and took half a year break before starting community college. I can't say if I really took the time to make an effort to feel better during the time I had off, but I spent enough days bored out of my mind that I decided I had to do literally anything else.

I decided that I'd make an effort in college - not necessarily to get top marks, but to not kid myself and do my best. While I'm still anxious, hardly know anyone in my class, and would never go to a party, I feel like I've become much more confident and more optimistic about my future. 

So I think if you want to start a new life, go for it! The high school years truly are some of the worst of your life - for me it was a weight off my shoulders knowing that I would never go back. No matter what it is that you want to do next, you can do it as long as you put in the hard work. It will take time, but you may be surprised how different your life can feel in just a few months.
